title: Medication & IV Safety
html:
Safe medication care is a reasoning process: verify the order, client, medication, dose, route, timing, allergies, indication, relevant assessment, and monitoring plan. Technology supports these checks but does not replace judgment.

Stop at uncertainty

  • Hold and clarify an incomplete, illegible, contraindicated, or unexpectedly dosed order.
  • Use independent verification for high-alert medications when policy requires it.
  • Know what effect and adverse response you are monitoring before administration.
After administration
Document accurately and reassess the outcome. A medication is not safely given until the client's response is considered.

Watch the access site and the client

For parenteral therapy, assess line patency, site condition, compatibility, rate, and systemic response. If infiltration, extravasation, reaction, or overload is suspected, stop or pause the source as appropriate, assess, and follow the medication- and facility-specific protocol.

Reconcile transitions

Compare what the client was taking with new orders at admission, transfer, and discharge. Resolve duplications, omissions, interactions, and unclear instructions before they reach the client.
